frequency_question: How often do central bank regulatory boards complete a multi-step analytical, proposal, notice-and-comment, and finalization process to raise the countercyclical capital buffer above zero within a defined calendar horizon?
membership_rule: Includes all formal regulatory proposals by major central banks to activate or raise a countercyclical capital buffer rate from 0% to a positive level. Excludes routine microprudential capital adjustments or monetary policy interest rate decisions.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB Activation 2018
Swiss National Bank / FINMA CCyB Activation 2012-2014

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major international implementations named; forms the complete set of early-adopter jurisdiction framework activations.
known_gaps: Limited to jurisdictions that have actually activated the buffer; the U.S. Federal Reserve has maintained its buffer at 0% historically, meaning structural template matching relies on peer central banks.
skeleton: Regulatory cycles across 5 major jurisdictions implementing macroprudential frameworks, multiplied by the average administrative duration of 6 to 9 months per rule-making cycle.
multiplier: 5 jurisdiction cycles observed, all successfully completing the required procedural steps within a 12-month window once initiated.
validity_reason: Administrative rulemaking procedures for central banks change slowly over decades, maintaining structural validity through the decade.
